Hypothesis: Bronze B was cast/produced broadly within the 5th century BC.
Operational note: Broad chronology only; does not assert a fine stylistic date.

Hypothesis: A and B differ in production date by roughly the stylistically expected multi-decade interval.
Operational note: Current AMS resolution may be insufficient to test this directly.

Hypothesis: Bronze B's welding metal reflects a distinct and possibly later welding episode.

Hypothesis: The tenon lead of A and B shares a Greek-source isotopic signature.
Operational note: Does not by itself prove the exact place/date of installation.

Hypothesis: Bronze B welding/restoration material is geochemically compatible with CIANE/Pantanelli sediments from the Syracuse area.

Hypothesis: The bronzes experienced a multi-phase marine depositional/alteration history.

Hypothesis: Bronze B's principal casting-core material derives from the Sibari area / northern Calabria.

Hypothesis: Bronze A's principal casting-core material derives from Argos/Argolid.

Hypothesis: Bronze B's principal casting-core material derives from Argos/Argolid.

Hypothesis: Bronze A's principal casting-core material derives broadly from southern Greece.

Hypothesis: Bronze B's principal casting-core material derives broadly from southern Greece.

Hypothesis: Bronze B's principal casting-core material derives from Athens/Attica.
